ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 conclusion] The statement writes (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + deltab; [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: proof chain] the proof obtains x_hat = (A + DeltaA)^dagger(b + deltab).
ambiguities.impact: The source unambiguously supports that x_hat is a pseudoinverse least-squares solution of the perturbed problem. Exact equality of the tall linear system additionally requires b + deltab to lie in the range of A + DeltaA, which is not stated.
ambiguities.issue: The theorem's literal perturbed equation and the proof's pseudoinverse relation are not equivalent for a general inconsistent overdetermined right-hand side.

ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 bound] Only ||DeltaA||_2 is bounded; [PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: moral of Theorem 3.5] small relative deltab is imposed separately in the interpretation; [PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: equation (1.2)] the earlier normwise backward error eta_F is a joint Frobenius minimization over perturbations to A and b.
ambiguities.impact: The passage must not be translated as an unconditional bound on eta_F or as a theorem that deltab is small.
ambiguities.issue: The paper uses "backward error" here while bounding only the absolute spectral norm of DeltaA.

ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: Theorem 3.4 opening] It prints S in R^{s x n} while also forming SA with A in R^{m x n}; [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 opening] Theorem 3.5 prints the consistent S in R^{s x m}; [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909; anchor: Algorithm 1.3] the algorithm also uses S in R^{s x m}.
ambiguities.impact: The source contract uses s-by-m for Theorem 3.5 and records the Theorem 3.4 occurrence as a typographical ambiguity rather than importing it.
ambiguities.issue: The cross-referenced Theorem 3.4 contains a dimensionally inconsistent type for S.

ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: Theorem 3.4 conclusion] Y_hat itself is full rank through its finite condition-number bound; [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] no explicit smallness or rank-preservation condition is imposed on DeltaY_hat before the proof writes (R_hat + DeltaR_hat)^{-1}(Y_hat + DeltaY_hat)^dagger = (A + DeltaA)^dagger.
ambiguities.impact: The intended small-backward-error regime would preserve rank, but the theorem passage does not state that prerequisite explicitly.
ambiguities.issue: The proof's product-pseudoinverse identity implicitly needs suitable rank conditions on Y_hat + DeltaY_hat.

contract_plain_english: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: definition of DeltaA and following estimate] Conditional on LSQR admitting the stated perturbed pseudoinverse representation, SAA Blendenpik composes the error in forming Y_hat, the LSQR matrix perturbation, and the final triangular-solve perturbation into an exact four-term DeltaA, including the mixed product, and bounds its spectral norm by the displayed expression with both n and sqrt(n) factors.

source_evidence.observation: Theorem 3.5 applies Algorithm 1.3 under assumptions (3.6)-(3.7) and assumes LSQR returns z_hat = (Y_hat + DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b + deltab).

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 3.5, definition of DeltaA
source_evidence.observation: The proof defines DeltaA exactly as (Y_hat R_hat - A) + DeltaY_hat R_hat + Y_hat DeltaR_hat + DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat.

source_evidence.anchor: Rowwise triangular-solve relation in the proof of Theorem 3.5
source_evidence.observation: Each row satisfies y_hat_i^T R_hat - a_i^T = -y_hat_i^T Delta_i R_hat with |Delta_i R_hat| <= gamma_n |R_hat|, yielding ||Y_hat R_hat - A||_2 <= n gamma_n ||R_hat||_2 ||Y_hat||_2.

source_evidence.anchor: Immediate compositional norm bound after the definition of DeltaA
Continuation of the proof of Theorem 3.5
source_evidence.observation: Substitution of bounds on R_hat and Y_hat gives the theorem's explicit estimate with constants 6.04 and 2.01.
The referenced assumptions are kappa_2(SQ_A) < 49, n^2 u < 1/201, m/n + sqrt(n) > 200, and kappa_2(A) < 1/(3 C_1 k(S)).
C_1 and k(S) are defined by C_1 = sqrt(sn) gamma_m + sqrt(n) tilde-gamma_{sn}(1 + sqrt(sn) gamma_m) and k(S) = ||S||_2 ||(SQ_A)^dagger||_2.
SAA Blendenpik forms B = SA, obtains R by Householder QR, computes Y = AR^{-1} by forward substitution, runs unpreconditioned LSQR on Yz = b, and computes x = R^{-1}z by back substitution.
The standard rounding constant is gamma_n = nu/(1-nu), with entrywise absolute-value inequalities interpreted componentwise.
Back substitution produces a perturbation DeltaR_hat satisfying (R_hat + DeltaR_hat)x_hat = z_hat and ||DeltaR_hat||_2 <= gamma_n sqrt(n)||R_hat||_2.

statement.algorithm_linkage: [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909; anchor: Algorithm 1.3] The linked algorithm draws S, computes B = SA and its Householder-QR triangular factor R, explicitly computes Y = AR^{-1} by forward substitution, solves Yz = b with unpreconditioned LSQR, and computes x = R^{-1}z by back substitution; [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: section 3.4 opening] the analyzed variant omits SAS initialization.
binders: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 statement] A is in R^{m x n}, S is in R^{s x m}, b is in R^m, z_hat and x_hat are in R^n, and the algorithm produces computed matrices R_hat in R^{n x n} and Y_hat in R^{m x n}.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] DeltaY_hat in R^{m x n} and deltab in R^m are perturbations witnessing the assumed LSQR backward-error representation.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: final triangular solve and DeltaA definition] DeltaR_hat is the backward perturbation for the final triangular solve, Delta_i R_hat is the separate rowwise perturbation used when Y_hat was formed, and DeltaA is an m-by-n perturbation defined in the proof.
conclusions: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: proof chain for x_hat] The proof states x_hat = (R_hat + DeltaR_hat)^{-1}z_hat = (R_hat + DeltaR_hat)^{-1}(Y_hat + DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b + deltab) = (A + DeltaA)^dagger(b + deltab).

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: displayed definition of DeltaA] DeltaA = (Y_hat R_hat - A) + DeltaY_hat R_hat + Y_hat DeltaR_hat + DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat, equivalently A + DeltaA = (Y_hat + DeltaY_hat)(R_hat + DeltaR_hat).

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: rowwise relation] For each row i, y_hat_i^T R_hat - a_i^T = -y_hat_i^T Delta_i R_hat and |Delta_i R_hat| <= gamma_n|R_hat|, hence ||Y_hat R_hat - A||_2 <= n gamma_n||R_hat||_2||Y_hat||_2.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: immediate compositional estimate] ||DeltaA||_2 <= ||R_hat||_2((n + sqrt(n))gamma_n||Y_hat||_2 + (1 + sqrt(n)gamma_n)||DeltaY_hat||_2).

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 conclusion] The theorem literally describes the perturbed relation as (A + DeltaA)x_hat = b + deltab and gives ||DeltaA||_2 < ||S||_2||A||_2(6.04 n gamma_n||(SQ_A)^dagger||_2 + 2.01||DeltaY_hat||_2).

[PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: final line of the proof] Before combining the factor 2, the proof obtains ||DeltaA||_2 <= 2||S||_2||A||_2(3.02 n gamma_n||(SQ_A)^dagger||_2 + 1.005||DeltaY_hat||_2).
constants_and_indexing: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: immediate compositional estimate] The coefficients are exactly (n + sqrt(n))gamma_n and 1 + sqrt(n)gamma_n; neither n nor sqrt(n) may be dropped.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: displayed DeltaA expansion] The mixed term DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat is present with coefficient one.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 bound] The final theorem uses the strict bound with constants 6.04 and 2.01.
[PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: final proof estimate] The preceding non-strict estimate uses an outer factor 2 and constants 3.02 and 1.005.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: rowwise identity] The index i ranges over rows of A and Y_hat; each row may have a different perturbation Delta_i R_hat.
definitions_and_conventions: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] DeltaY_hat is the matrix perturbation in the assumed LSQR backward error, while deltab is its right-hand-side perturbation.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: footnote 5] DeltaY_hat is explicitly distinguished from DeltaY, the earlier finite-precision error in computing Y_hat = A R_hat^{-1}.
[PDF p. 10, printed p. 914; anchor: equation (2.1)] gamma_n := nu/(1-nu).
[PDF p. 13, printed p. 917; anchor: equation (3.4)] C_1 := sqrt(sn)gamma_m + sqrt(n)tilde-gamma_{sn}(1 + sqrt(sn)gamma_m), and k(S) := ||S||_2||(SQ_A)^dagger||_2.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 913; anchor: Lemma 2.1 notation] Q_A is an orthonormal basis for the column space of A, inherited from an economized QR factorization A = Q_A R_A.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: rowwise perturbation bound] Absolute-value bars in |Delta_i R_hat| <= gamma_n|R_hat| denote entrywise absolute values.
error_notions: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] The assumed LSQR error is a perturbed least-squares/pseudoinverse relation involving both DeltaY_hat and deltab.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: displayed definition of DeltaA] DeltaA composes four sources exactly: the error in reconstructing A from Y_hat R_hat, the LSQR matrix perturbation propagated through R_hat, the final triangular-solve perturbation propagated through Y_hat, and their product.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: immediate compositional estimate] The selected estimate is an absolute spectral-norm bound on DeltaA, not a relative bound and not the joint Frobenius backward error eta_F.
[PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: moral of Theorem 3.5] The theorem gives no numerical bound on deltab; the later backward-stability interpretation separately requires ||deltab||_2/||b||_2 = O(u).
exceptional_values: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: assumption n^2u < 1/201] The roundoff regime keeps the denominators used in the surrounding gamma-based estimates away from zero.
[PDF p. 11, printed p. 915; anchor: equation (2.6)] The final relation uses an invertible perturbed triangular factor R_hat + DeltaR_hat.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: theorem and proof] No model for overflow, underflow, NaNs, infinities, or subnormal values is stated.
higher_order_terms: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: displayed definition of DeltaA] The second-order product DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat is retained exactly rather than omitted.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: immediate compositional estimate] Its contribution is retained through the factor (1 + sqrt(n)gamma_n)||DeltaY_hat||_2; the selected estimate has no omitted big-O remainder.
[PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: moral of Theorem 3.5] O(u) appears only in the subsequent conditional interpretation of LSQR backward stability, not in the exact expansion or compositional bound.
hypotheses: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 opening] S and A satisfy assumptions (3.6) and (3.7) from Theorem 3.4, and Algorithm 1.3 is applied.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: equation (3.6)] Explicitly, kappa_2(SQ_A) < 49, n^2 u < 1/201, and m/n + sqrt(n) > 200.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: equation (3.7)] Explicitly, kappa_2(A) < 1/(3 C_1 k(S)).

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] Quantifier order is conditional on an LSQR termination iterate z_hat for which perturbations DeltaY_hat and deltab satisfy z_hat = (Y_hat + DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b + deltab).
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 906; anchor: standing full-rank assumption] The inherited least-squares setting takes A and SA to have full column rank and m > s > n.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: paragraph before Theorem 3.5] The analysis excludes SAS initialization and is stated to consider stability from any starting point.
implicit_context: [PDF p. 5, printed p. 909; anchor: Algorithm 1.3] This is the sketch-and-apply, not sketch-and-precondition, variant: LSQR is unpreconditioned and operates on the explicitly formed Y.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 918; anchor: Theorem 3.4 conclusion] Under the inherited assumptions, the previously established result is kappa_2(Y_hat) <= 4kappa_2(SQ_A) + 1.

[PDF p. 17, printed p. 921; anchor: paragraph following Theorem 3.5] The paper interprets the result as backward stability only if LSQR itself supplies ||DeltaY_hat||_2 = O(u) and ||deltab||_2/||b||_2 = O(u); that LSQR property is not proved by Theorem 3.5.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: bounds following the compositional estimate] The proof uses ||R_hat||_2 < 2||S||_2||A||_2 and ||Y_hat||_2 < 1.51||(SQ_A)^dagger||_2 to reach the numerical constants in the theorem.
norms: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Theorem 3.5 and proof estimates] Norms on DeltaA, R_hat, Y_hat, DeltaY_hat, S, A, and (SQ_A)^dagger are spectral matrix 2-norms.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: rowwise perturbation relation] The bound on Delta_i R_hat is componentwise, whereas the resulting bounds on Y_hat R_hat - A and DeltaA are spectral-norm bounds.
numerical_model: [PDF p. 10, printed p. 914; anchor: equation (2.1)] Arithmetic uses unit roundoff u and gamma_n = nu/(1-nu) for standard componentwise rounding bounds.
[PDF p. 11, printed p. 915; anchor: equation (2.6)] The final back substitution is backward stable in the stated model, producing ||DeltaR_hat||_2 <= gamma_n sqrt(n)||R_hat||_2.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: rowwise relation for Y_hat R_hat - A] Formation of Y_hat is represented by distinct row-dependent perturbations Delta_i R_hat bounded componentwise.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] Numerical behavior of LSQR is not derived from the rounding model; its backward-error representation is an additional assumption.

undebatable_constraints: [PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: displayed definition of DeltaA] DeltaA must contain all four terms, including both Y_hat R_hat - A and the mixed product DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat.

[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: immediate compositional estimate] The requested norm estimate is spectral and has exactly ||R_hat||_2((n+sqrt(n))gamma_n||Y_hat||_2 + (1+sqrt(n)gamma_n)||DeltaY_hat||_2).
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: equation (3.9)] The result is conditional on an LSQR backward-error representation; it does not prove that LSQR supplies small DeltaY_hat or deltab.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: footnote 5] DeltaY_hat must not be identified with the earlier forward-substitution error DeltaY.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: Algorithm 1.3 linkage in section 3.4] The algorithm variant is SAA Blendenpik with explicitly formed Y and unpreconditioned LSQR, without SAS initialization.
[PDF p. 16, printed p. 920; anchor: theorem conclusion] A faithful contract must preserve deltab in the perturbed-data relation even though the theorem's displayed bound controls only DeltaA.
